relations.quote: Truncation is taken over pairs chosen by their [addresses](address.md), one rounding per layer.

symbols.name: precision
symbols.meaning: The number of fractional binary places kept, which counts the binary digits after the point.
symbols.quote: Let $p$ be the number of fractional binary places kept, so the grid spacing is $2^{-p}$.

symbols.name: coefficient list
symbols.meaning: A finite list of complex numbers, called coefficients.
symbols.quote: Let $w$ be a finite list of complex numbers, called coefficients.

symbols.name: truncation operator
symbols.meaning: The map that truncates each real and imaginary part of each coefficient toward zero onto the grid $2^{-p}\mathbb{Z}$.
symbols.quote: Then $Q_p w$ is the list obtained by truncating each real and imaginary part of each coefficient toward zero onto the grid $2^{-p}\mathbb{Z}$, where $\mathbb{Z}$ is the set of [integers](integer.md).

symbols.name: integers
symbols.meaning: The set of integers, whose multiples of $2^{-p}$ form the truncation grid.
symbols.quote: Then $Q_p w$ is the list obtained by truncating each real and imaginary part of each coefficient toward zero onto the grid $2^{-p}\mathbb{Z}$, where $\mathbb{Z}$ is the set of [integers](integer.md).

symbols.name: array norm
symbols.meaning: The largest complex modulus of any coefficient in an array.
symbols.quote: The error is measured by the [Array norm](array-norm.md) $\|\cdot\|_\infty$, the largest complex modulus of any coefficient.

symbols.name: layer
symbols.meaning: The map that replaces each pair of values $s$ and $r$ by $((s+r)/2,(s-r)/2)$, applied to every pair of entries whose addresses differ in one of several selected bits.
symbols.quote: A layer, written $H$, is one pass that replaces each pair of values $s$ and $r$ by $((s+r)/2,(s-r)/2)$, for every pair of entries whose [addresses](address.md) differ in one of several selected bits.

symbols.name: first pair value
symbols.meaning: The first of the two values in a pair that a layer combines.
symbols.quote: A layer, written $H$, is one pass that replaces each pair of values $s$ and $r$ by $((s+r)/2,(s-r)/2)$, for every pair of entries whose [addresses](address.md) differ in one of several selected bits.

symbols.name: second pair value
symbols.meaning: The second of the two values in a pair that a layer combines.
symbols.quote: A layer, written $H$, is one pass that replaces each pair of values $s$ and $r$ by $((s+r)/2,(s-r)/2)$, for every pair of entries whose [addresses](address.md) differ in one of several selected bits.
